name: Olympic Movement (1920–1986)
description: A white field charged at the centre with five interlaced rings — blue, yellow, black, green and red — in two rows, drawn as continuous interlocking rings.
history: Pierre de Coubertin's rings, designed in 1913 and presented in June 1914, were first flown at the Antwerp Games of 1920. This original rendering, with the rings fully interlaced, was used until 1986, when the IOC's graphic standards introduced a version with visible gaps between the rings.

features.role: five interlaced rings in blue, yellow, black, green and red
features.symbolism: the five inhabited continents united by Olympism; colours chosen so that every national flag contains at least one
